themes_detail.label: Construction Surge & Plumbing Crisis
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 44 THIS WEEK versus 12.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (245% increase, z-score 8.15), suggesting either a major building project, widespread infrastructure failure, or contractor influx tied to the five active ULURP rezonings in the pipeline.
evidence: 44 construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs 12.8 weekly baseline (245% spike, z-score 8.15)
316 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (237 alterations, 32 new buildings, 9 demolitions)
Five active ULURP/rezoning applications in review (1455 Coney Island Ave, 2586 Nostrand Ave, 1584 Flatbush Ave, two historic district reviews)
reporting_angles: Are contractors tied to pending rezonings creating neighborhood disruption before projects even break ground?
Is the city's plumbing infrastructure failing under construction pressure, or are illegitimate contractors flooding the district?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints hit 5 THIS WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score 4.66), marking the most dramatic surge in the dataset and signaling either a new homeless encampment cluster or rapid deterioration of street conditions in specific blocks.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score 4.66, highest z-score in dataset)
No prior reporting or community board mentions, suggesting sudden emergence
Concurrent 138% noise spike (25 complaints last week vs 10.5 avg) may indicate concentrated encampment activity
reporting_angles: Where are these encampments located, and what triggered the sudden spike this week?
Are social services or NYPD outreach teams aware, and what interventions are planned?

themes_detail.label: Dumpster & Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints surged to 4 three weeks ago (3100% spike, z-score 11.72) and residential disposal complaints hit 23 two weeks ago (300% spike, z-score 5.1), indicating a coordinated sanitation breakdown—possibly tied to construction debris or contractor mismanagement.
evidence: 4 dumpster complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72, second-highest in dataset)
23 residential disposal complaints 2 weeks ago vs 5.8 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score 5.1)
Concurrent 245% construction spike suggests contractor-generated debris overload
reporting_angles: Are construction projects illegally dumping or failing to manage site debris?
Is DSNY overwhelmed by disposal volume, or are specific blocks the focus?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Escalate
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 25 last week versus 10.5 weekly average (138% spike, z-score 4.53), the third-largest complaint category overall (1,910 over 90 days), likely driven by construction activity tied to rezoning applications.
evidence: 25 noise complaints last week vs 10.5 weekly baseline (138% spike, z-score 4.53)
Noise is the third-highest complaint category overall (1,910 complaints over 90 days)
Spike correlates with construction complaint surge (44 THIS WEEK vs 12.8 baseline)
reporting_angles: Which blocks are experiencing the worst noise, and what are the sources (construction, contractors, street work)?
Are permits for noisy work being granted without resident notification?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 11 three weeks ago (214% increase, z-score 7.5), potentially signaling heating system failures, mold issues, or construction-related contamination affecting residential spaces.
evidence: 11 indoor air quality complaints 3 weeks ago vs 3.5 weekly baseline (214% spike, z-score 7.5)
Concurrent heat/hot water complaints remain extremely high (5,494 over 90 days, largest category)
Construction activity surge may be generating dust or air quality issues
reporting_angles: Are landlords failing to maintain heating/ventilation systems during winter, or is construction contaminating residential buildings?
Are vulnerable populations (elderly, children, immunocompromised) being affected?
